data.narrative:
Outrider is a Series D robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $262M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of nine peers spanning public and private markets: one public company (277810.KQ) and eight private firms including Exotec, Divergent, Locus Robotics, Bedrock Robotics, and Dexterity. The peer set includes companies across Series C through Series E stages.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a proxy baseline, applies a typical 1.5x step-up multiplier from Series D forward, yielding an implied valuation of $393M. Peer-median methodology draws from four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables: Divergent ($2.3B, Series E), Exotec ($2.0B, Series D), Hadrian ($1.6B, Series C), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B, Series C). The median across these four yields $1.8B, with a range of $1.0B to $2.3B.

Triangulation across both methods supports a valuation range of $334M (low) to $2.1B (high), with a median of $1.1B. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around stage-comparable benchmarking and peer selection sensitivity. The stage-progression method generates substantial underweighting relative to peer valuations, likely due to the raised-capital proxy not capturing company-specific unit economics or market position. Key uncertainties include peer comparability on revenue scale and growth trajectory, and whether recent market conditions have compressed multiples across the robotics sector.
